- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >82), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; cap forecast at +5% above peak or use 3-day moving average for smoothing.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is falling, model underestimates; add 1–2% buffer to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently overreacts to sentiment shifts — if sentiment flips from bullish to bearish, delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days to avoid lagged correction.
- In early forecast windows (e.g., 30d), model often misses late-stage trend reversals; anchor forecast to 7–14 day moving average if sentiment is volatile.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending, model tends to lag; add 1–2 day lead to forecast to capture momentum.
- If sentiment is high and price is near 85+, model often overestimates; cap forecast at 87–88 unless sentiment is strongly bullish with strong momentum.
